title: Linking computational budget to certified safety margins for robot fault tolerant control
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF DYNAMICS AND CONTROL
robot_model: KUKA LBR iiwa (PyBullet kuka_iiwa URDF); also double integrator and simple pendulum testbeds
fault_equation: u_actual = diag(theta) u_cmd, theta_i in [theta_min, 1], theta_min = 1 - delta_max
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_i = theta_i, b_i = 0, s_i = 0, box bound u in [u_min, u_max]
fault_magnitude: KUKA: theta_true ~ U(0.4, 1.0) per trial; double integrator: theta_true ~ U(0.5, 1.0), delta_max = 0.5 (up to 0.85 in sensitivity)
onset: NR (constant fault over the run)
mechanism: anytime RLS effectiveness estimator; CBF-QP safety filter using theta_hat with a confidence-radius additive margin that shrinks with compute budget
detection_delay: budget-dependent T_detect from RLS covariance; certificate covers the window before detection
structural_condition: single faulty actuator per channel, full actuation remains with reduced effectiveness; u_max = 180 N m on KUKA joint
platform: PyBullet physics engine (KUKA iiwa URDF), Python
baselines: no-FTC; passive FTC (worst-case margin); naive active FTC (fixed trigger); BFTC-binary; adaptive MIT-rule FTC; robust MPC-FTC
metric: safety violation rate and mean minimum barrier value h_min; mean velocity fraction (double integrator)
repetitions: 40 trials per strategy (KUKA), 150 per cell (double integrator); McNemar tests and paired effect sizes
notes: Main testbed is a double integrator; manipulator is a 7-DOF PyBullet KUKA with one joint actuated. No fault-free reference run reported. Code repository promised upon acceptance.

title: A Simulative Study on Model-Based Emergency Strategies for Damage Prevention After Cable Breaks in Cable-Driven Parallel Robots
robot_model: SEGESTA cable-driven parallel robot
fault_equation: cable break: force of the broken cable k set to zero (f_k = 0), its column removed from the structure matrix, A_r f_r + w_e = M_P xdd + ... (Eqs. 33-34)
normal_form_fit: partial: total loss of one cable channel corresponds to lambda_k = 0, b_k = 0 on that actuator (transmission break); no joint-level constraint
fault_magnitude: complete break of cable 4 (force = 0)
onset: NR (break at start of each run from static equilibrium)
mechanism: post-break emergency motion with remaining cables: energy-minimizing NMPC, potential-field trajectory to a safe pose, cable force distribution beyond the wrench-feasible workspace, and their hybrid
structural_condition: 7 of 8 cables remain; platform leaves the wrench-feasible workspace, recovery not always possible (about 58 % maximum success)
platform: MATLAB Simulink multibody model of SEGESTA with actuator dynamics, cable elasticity, pulley and winch kinematics
baselines: two state-of-the-art strategies (EMM with short horizon, PFM-NCM) against novel variants (EMM-H5, PFM-ECF, EMM-ECF, EMM-PFM)
metric: success rate over 1000 runs; computation time; crash kinetic energy; wrench RMSE
repetitions: 1000 simulations with random initial poses per strategy
notes: Simulation only; success rate 58.2 % (EMM-H5), 57.7 % (EMM-PFM), 55.9 % (EMM-ECF). No fault-free run. Data not available (NDA).

title: Adaptive Nonsingular Predefined-Time Sliding Mode Fault Tolerant Control for Manipulator System With Given Steady-State Error
robot_model: 2-link planar
fault_equation: tau = rho u + varpi, rho = diag{rho_i(t)}, rho_i(t) in [rho_0, 1], varpi_i(t) bounded additive fault
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_i = rho_i(t) (time-varying), b_i = varpi_i(t), s_i = 0
fault_magnitude: rho = diag{0.5 + 0.2 sin(0.01 t), 0.7 + 0.3 sin(0.01 t)}; further fault cases in Table 2 (image)
onset: NR (fault acts over the whole run)
mechanism: adaptive nonsingular predefined-time sliding mode control; adaptive gain compensates the lumped fault and disturbance bound
structural_condition: partial loss on both joints; full actuation remains
platform: NR (numerical simulation of a 2-link arm)
baselines: predefined-time sliding mode controller of ref. [44]
metric: tracking error norm (plots only)
repetitions: single runs for several convergence times, initial states, fault cases and disturbance types; no statistics
notes: E_AMBIG: section titled Experimental Results but only a numerical 2-link model is described (also called simulation results). Disturbance d = [0.1 + 0.1 sin(0.01 t), 0.2 + 0.1 sin(0.01 t)]. No fault-free run, no numerical metric.

title: Novel Finite-Time Adaptive Fuzzy Fault-Tolerant Control for Fractional-Order Nonlinear Systems and Its Applications
robot_model: Quanser rotary flexible link (single-link flexible manipulator), QLabs virtual model
fault_equation: u(t) = psi mu(t) + vartheta (u_bar - psi mu(t)); lock-in-place u_j(t) = u_bar_j for t >= t_j; loss of effectiveness u_j(t) = psi_j mu_j(t), psi_j in (psi_low, 1]
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_j = psi_j, s_j = vartheta_j, tau_bar_j = u_bar_j (stuck-at input), b_j = 0
fault_magnitude: manipulator: psi = 0.7 for t > 5 s; numerical examples: stuck values u = 2, 3, 6, psi from 0.5 + 0.1 cos(x1 x2) to 0.2
onset: t = 5 s (manipulator); 4 s, 8 s and other switching times in numerical examples
mechanism: finite-time adaptive fuzzy backstepping with fractional-order dynamic surface control; adaptive laws absorb fault and disturbance bounds
structural_condition: single actuator; only loss of effectiveness admissible (no more than q - 1 stuck actuators)
platform: Quanser QLabs virtual flexible link with MATLAB Simulink and Quarc
baselines: adaptive fuzzy FTC with infinite-time convergence (numerical example only)
metric: tracking error (plots only)
repetitions: single run per scenario; no statistics
notes: E_AMBIG: section titled Experiment uses the QLabs virtual model (stated equivalent to the Quanser hardware); no physical run reported. Main plant is a generic fractional-order system; numerical examples include a power system. Comparison with AFFTC only in a numerical example.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Prescribed-Time Fault-Tolerant Fuzzy Optimal Tracking Control for Stochastic Nonlinear Systems and Its Application to Robot Arm
journal: IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON SYSTEMS MAN CYBERNETICS-SYSTEMS
robot_model: single-link arm driven by a brushed DC motor (electromechanical benchmark)
fault_equation: vartheta_k(t) = (1 - theta_k) eta_k u_k(t) + theta_k vartheta_bar_k; LIP vartheta_j(t) = vartheta_bar_j for t >= t_j; LIE vartheta_k = eta_k u_k for t >= t_k; system fault G(t) H(z) with G(t) = 0 for t < T_fault, 1 otherwise
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_k = eta_k, s_k = theta_k, tau_bar_k = vartheta_bar_k; system fault H(z) enters the electrical state equation as an additive term (b, state dependent)
fault_magnitude: eta_1 = 0.78 (22 % loss) for t > 6 s; actuator 2 stuck at a constant output (theta_2 = 1); H(z) = 5 z2 sin(z1) from T_fault = 15 s
onset: t = 6 s (actuator faults); T_fault = 15 s (system fault)
mechanism: fuzzy identifier-critic-actor reinforcement learning with predefined-time prescribed-performance backstepping; learning laws estimate fault effects and compensate
structural_condition: two redundant input channels (alpha = [1, 2]); one stuck, one partially effective
platform: NR (numerical simulation)
baselines: AFTC [17], PTFTC [22], AFTC [30], FTFTC [39], FTFTC [43]; different predefined times
metric: tracking error, convergence time and control input (Table II); cost function reduction about 25-30 %
repetitions: single run per scheme; no statistics
notes: Stochastic Ito system with Gaussian white-noise torque and control disturbances. Generic stochastic nonlinear system, single-link arm as application. Table II is an image (convergence time and input).

title: A new hybrid neurodynamics-based model-less solution for redundant robot fault-tolerant motion planning and control
robot_model: Kinova Jaco Gen3 (experiment); Kinova Jaco Gen2 (simulation)
fault_equation: qd_ft1 = ... = qd_ft_tau = 0 for the faulty joints; fault state matrix M qd = 0 as equality constraint in the QP
normal_form_fit: full: joint-level constraint qd_i = 0 (locked joint)
fault_magnitude: joint 3 locked, or joints 3 and 5 locked, at the initial configuration
onset: NR (joints faulty over the whole task)
mechanism: task-priority QP minimizing joint velocity with faulty-joint equality constraints, solved by finite-time zeroing neurodynamics; Jacobian estimated online by gradient neurodynamics (model-less)
structural_condition: kinematic redundancy (6- and 7-DOF arms, 3-D position task); one or two locked joints
platform: Kinova Jaco Gen3 with binocular camera; simulation of Kinova Jaco Gen2
injection: software command (faulty joint velocity set to zero)
baselines: fault-free run; model-based FTC of ref. [3] with DH parameter bias; model-free DMFFTC of ref. [29]
metric: RMSE of end-effector tracking (mm)
repetitions: single run per scenario; no statistics
notes: Simulation RMSE 3.71e-2 mm (q3 fault) vs 4.95e-2 mm DMFFTC; two faults 4.21e-2 vs 6.26e-2 mm. Experiment RMSE 0.3927 and 0.3954 mm. HTML body not served through the proxy; publisher PDF read.

title: Reinforcement-Learning-Based Finite Time Fault Tolerant Control for a Manipulator With Actuator Faults
robot_model: Kinova Jaco 2 (lightweight cooperative arm); 2-link planar in simulation
fault_equation: tau = D(t) u + u0, D(t) = diag{d_1(t),...,d_n(t)}, d_i(t) in (0,1]; lumped fault (D(t) - I) u + u0
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_i = d_i(t) (time-varying), b_i = u0_i, s_i = 0
fault_magnitude: simulation: d_2 = 0.5 on joint 2 for 2 < t < 10 s, u0 = [1, 1] N m on all joints; experiment: d_1 = 0.1 to 1 in steps of 0.1 on joint 1 during 20-30 s
onset: t = 2 s (simulation, removed at 10 s); t = 20 s (experiment, removed at 30 s)
mechanism: nonsingular terminal sliding mode with adaptive anti-fault compensator (adaptive gain, sign term); actor-critic NN approximates unknown dynamics and cost
structural_condition: partial loss on one joint; full actuation remains
platform: Kinova Jaco 2 driven from MATLAB; MATLAB simulation of a 2-link arm
baselines: simulation: PD and five FTC/adaptive controllers from refs [22], [27], [28], [38], [39]; experiment: no comparison controller (effectiveness levels only, d = 1 as fault-free)
metric: mean absolute tracking error PI_i (rad); CPU time
repetitions: single run per case; no statistics
notes: Experiment Table V: joint 1 mean error 0.41e-2 (d = 1) to 1.88e-2 rad (d = 0.1). Simulation Table III: PI_1 0.0343 (proposed) vs 0.0645 (PD). Fault-free reference only in experiment; comparison with alternatives only in simulation. RL treats dynamics, fault handled by adaptive compensator.

title: Intelligent Fault-Tolerant Control of Delta Robots: A Hybrid Optimization Approach for Enhanced Trajectory Tracking
robot_model: four-arm Delta parallel robot (authors' design, Schneider BCH2 servomotors)
fault_equation: NR (verbal: breakdown of actuator 3 causing loss of control of that joint; fault in position sensor of motor 2; both combined)
normal_form_fit: partial: actuator breakdown (electrical disconnection) corresponds to lambda_3 = 0, b_3 = 0, but no equation is written; sensor fault form not given
fault_magnitude: NR (complete actuator 3 breakdown; sensor fault size not given)
onset: NR
mechanism: fault diagnosis (wavelet scattering, PCA, LDA, meta-learning, classifiers) triggers reconfiguration of interval type-2 fuzzy controller scaling factors by genetic algorithm plus gradient descent
detection_delay: diagnosis at the end of each 15 s trajectory cycle (68-93 ms processing), reconfiguration about 0.52 s
structural_condition: one of four actuators lost in a 3-DOF four-arm Delta (actuation redundancy); sensor and multiple faults also
platform: MATLAB simulation of a SolidWorks-designed Delta robot
baselines: same IT2 fuzzy controller before reconfiguration; fault-tolerant sliding mode controller
metric: ISE and ITAE of end-effector residual per axis, normalized degradation levels
repetitions: single 15 s run per fault scenario for FTC; diagnosis data from four trajectories with 5-fold cross-validation
notes: OWN (Urrea co-author). Multiple fault moved from critical to moderate degradation level after reconfiguration. Data stated as contained in the article.

title: Energy-Efficient and Fault-Tolerant Control of a Six-Axis Robot Based on AI Models
robot_model: Mitsubishi RV-12SDL
fault_equation: NR (verbal: the angular position of a failed or blocked axis does not change)
normal_form_fit: partial: joint-level constraint qd_i = 0 for the failed axis stated verbally, no equation
fault_magnitude: any one or any two of six axes locked (22 kinematic configurations); example: axis j3 locked
onset: NR (axis locked from the start of the task)
mechanism: stepwise motion replanning with the remaining axes; MLP selects active-axis configuration and reward parameters (trained on genetic-algorithm data) for energy-optimal obstacle-avoiding path
detection_delay: NR (failure declared when model-robot axis position error exceeds 0.05 deg at a step)
structural_condition: kinematic redundancy of a 6-axis arm for a positioning task; with two locked axes some targets unreachable
platform: MuJoCo model plus real Mitsubishi RV-12SDL with phase-current energy measurement
injection: software command (axis blocked in the controller)
baselines: all axes active versus locked-axis configurations; reward parameters from a different configuration
metric: energy consumed (Ws) and path length (m)
repetitions: 10 environmental situations x 22 configurations; 50 trials for torque-model accuracy (mean error 5.8 %)
notes: M1K1: 1.809 m, 1091 Ws with all axes; with j3 damaged 1.894 m, 1066 Ws. Accommodation is replanning with the remaining axes, aimed at energy saving. Data stated as contained in the article.

title: A sensorless approach for cable failure detection and identification in cable-driven parallel robots
robot_model: cable-suspended parallel robot prototype, University of Padova (B&R servo gear motors, Beckhoff drives)
fault_equation: cable break: structure matrix S (n x m) becomes n x (m - 1); actuator of the broken cable sees no tension, c_f = j_m,f thetadd_f + friction (Eq. 18)
normal_form_fit: partial: total loss of one cable channel corresponds to lambda_k = 0, b_k = 0 (transmission break); actuator itself remains healthy
fault_magnitude: complete break of cable 4 (electromagnet release)
onset: failure at the segment midpoint, e.g. t = 8.390 s, 4.850 s; t = 5.87 s in the recovery test
mechanism: sensorless detection and identification by comparing commanded torques with a digital twin (threshold 0.3 N m), then recovery with the remaining cables: tension-space polynomial motion to a safe point inside the residual static equilibrium workspace, then linear motion
detection_delay: measured: 60 ms (motion along the cable) to 200 ms (orthogonal motion); 190 ms in the recovery test
structural_condition: 3 of 4 cables remain; robot still fully actuated for a 3-DOF point mass within the residual workspace
platform: industrial-grade CSPR prototype; Simulink model and digital twin
baselines: pre-failure segment of the same run; no alternative recovery method compared
metric: detection time; digital twin agreement KPIs (Kj 0.0583 rad, Kt 0.1566 N m); end-effector trajectory to safe point
repetitions: 8 motion directions x 2 senses for detection (single run each); one recovery test
notes: Detection and identification correct in all tests. Recovery tested once on a circular trajectory; positive cable tensions maintained. Digital twin used for detection (T_DT).

title: Robust Adaptive Fuzzy Fault Tolerant Control of Robot Manipulators With Unknown Parameters
dof: 3 (UR5 first three joints, others locked); 3-link planar in simulation
robot_model: UR5; 3-link planar arm in simulation
fault_equation: u = xi u_F + delta(t), xi = diag(xi_i), xi_i in (0,1); plus process fault gamma(t - T_f) phi(q, qd) in the dynamics with gamma_i = 1 - exp(-rho_i (t - T_f)) for t >= T_f
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_i = xi_i (time-varying in validation), b_i = delta_i(t); process fault is an additional state-dependent term outside the actuator map
fault_magnitude: simulation 1: xi = 0.6 sin(t), delta = 0.3 for t >= 15 s, process fault with rho = 10, 30, 16; simulation 2: xi = 0.3 cos(t), delta = 0.8
onset: t = 15 s
profile: abrupt (actuator); exponential onset of process fault
mechanism: robust adaptive fuzzy control with zero-overshoot error constraint; adaptive robust term compensates actuator faults and approximation error
structural_condition: full actuation remains; time-varying gain and bias on all joints
platform: UR5 (three joints); MATLAB-type numerical simulation of 3-link arm
baselines: PID and NFTSMC; pre-fault segment of each run
metric: position tracking RMSE (Tables II, IV, V)
repetitions: single run per controller; no statistics
notes: Experiment faults stated to occur at t = 15 s with the same controller parameters; fault values in the experiment not restated. Friction and external disturbance in simulation. Input constraints not considered (stated).

title: Neural Network-Based Fixed-Time Tracking Control for Input-Quantized Nonlinear Systems With Actuator Faults
journal: IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON NEURAL NETWORKS AND LEARNING SYSTEMS
robot_model: single-link manipulator
fault_equation: q_f(u_j) = omega_jh q(u_j) + delta_jh(t) for t in [t_jh,k, t_jh,e), q(u_j) otherwise; omega_jh in [0,1]; PLOE: 0 < omega < 1, delta = 0; TLOE: omega = 0, delta != 0 (hysteresis quantizer q)
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_j = omega_jh, PLOE; TLOE as stuck-at time-varying output (s_j = 1, tau_bar_j = delta_jh(t)); intermittent switching; quantizer outside the normal form
fault_magnitude: u1: omega = 0, delta = 0.1 sin t (total loss); u2: omega = 0.5 (50 % loss), during [2k+1, 2k+2)
onset: t in [2k+1, 2k+2) for k = 0, 1, ... (first at t = 1 s)
mechanism: adaptive fixed-time backstepping with RBF neural approximation; adaptive estimates of upper bounds of quantization and fault parameters with auxiliary signals
structural_condition: two input channels; at most m - 1 actuators with total loss at once
platform: NR (numerical simulation)
baselines: none (fault-free intervals of the same run only)
metric: tracking plots only
repetitions: single run; no statistics
notes: Generic strict-feedback system with quantized inputs; single-link arm is the application example. Disturbance D2 = 0.1 sin t. No comparison controller, no numerical metric.

title: Integrated State/Fault Estimation and Fault-Tolerant Control Design for Switched T-S Fuzzy Systems With Sensor and Actuator Faults
robot_model: single-link flexible-joint manipulator driven by a DC motor
fault_equation: xdot = sum h_i [A_i x + B_i (u + F f_a) + E_i d]; y = C x + G f_s (manipulator: u_f(t) = u(t) + f_a(t))
normal_form_fit: full for the actuator fault: b = f_a(t) (time-varying), lambda = 1; sensor fault y = C x + G f_s outside the actuator map
fault_magnitude: manipulator: f_a = sin(0.7 pi (t - 5)), f_s = 2 sin(0.5 pi (t - 5)) for 5 <= t <= 30 s; Example 1: f_a = sin(t - 6), f_s = sin(0.4 pi (t - 6)) from 6 s
onset: t = 5 s (manipulator); t = 6 s (numerical example)
mechanism: switched T-S fuzzy observer estimates states and sensor and actuator faults; fuzzy controller subtracts the estimated actuator fault (integrated LMI design, H-infinity, MDADT)
structural_condition: single actuator; additive fault fully compensable
platform: NR (numerical simulation)
baselines: separated design (SD), two-step and single-step integrated designs; PI observer of ref. [37]
metric: state trajectories and fault estimates (plots); feasibility gamma values in Tables I and III
repetitions: single run per design; no statistics
notes: Generic switched T-S fuzzy system; single-link flexible-joint arm is Example 2. Tables report LMI feasibility (gamma, dwell time), not tracking metrics. Disturbance d = 0.2 sin(0.3 pi t).

title: Adaptive Iterative Learning Fault-Tolerant Control for State Constrained Nonlinear Systems With Randomly Varying Iteration Lengths
journal: IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON NEURAL NETWORKS AND LEARNING SYSTEMS
robot_model: single-link manipulator
fault_equation: u_i^F(t) = rho_i(t) u_i(t) + eta_i(t), 0 < rho_i(t) <= 1 (time- and iteration-dependent)
normal_form_fit: full: lambda = rho_i(t), b = eta_i(t), both time- and iteration-varying

platform: NR (numerical simulation)
baselines: PILC [24] and AILC [28]
metric: mean over iterations of maximum position and speed error E1, E2 (Tables I-IV)
repetitions: 30-40 learning iterations with random trial lengths; one simulation per case
notes: Iterative learning control across trials; generic SISO system with single-link arm as application. Load disturbance d = sin(pi t) + 0.01 rand in robustness case. No fault-free run.

title: Cooperative Fault-Tolerant Control for a Mobile Dual Flexible Manipulator With Output Constraints
journal: IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON AUTOMATION SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING
dof: 3 actuated (two joint motors and a mobile slider); flexible links (distributed parameter)
robot_model: mobile dual flexible manipulator grasping a rigid object
fault_equation: tau_i(t) = sigma_i tau_ci(t), u(t) = sigma u_c(t), sigma_i, sigma in (0, 1]

baselines: PD controllers
metric: maximum tip deflection (0.07 and 0.03 m vs 0.22 m PD), settling time, peak grasp force (4.5 N vs 25 N)
repetitions: single run; no statistics
notes: No fault-free run; the 50 % failure applies throughout. Boundary sensing of shear force and strain used in the control law (other).

title: Adaptive fuzzy terminal sliding mode control for the free-floating space manipulator with free-swinging joint failure
robot_model: SSRMS-type 7-DOF free-floating space manipulator
fault_equation: partitioned free-floating dynamics with passive (free-swinging) joints: tau_P = tau_f (friction only, then taken as 0), tau_b = 0; [M_b M_bP M_bA; M_Pb M_PP M_PA; M_Ab M_AP M_AA][qdd] + [c] = [0; 0 (or tau_f); tau_A]
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_i = 0, b_i = 0 on the passive joints (free-swinging)

platform: NR (numerical simulation)
baselines: TSMC with different switching gains versus AFTSMC
metric: passive joint convergence and active joint torque peak (3671.77 N m TSMC vs 1325.19 N m AFTSMC)
repetitions: single run per gain setting; no statistics
notes: No fault-free run. Only torque peaks reported numerically, no tracking error metric. Model uncertainty and sinusoidal torque disturbance included.

title: Sliding Mode Control for Robot Manipulators with Actuator Faults
journal: 2021 PROCEEDINGS OF THE 40TH CHINESE CONTROL CONFERENCE (CCC)
robot_model: 2-link planar rigid manipulator
fault_equation: u(t) = F(t) tau(t), F(t) = diag{f_1(t), ..., f_n(t)}, 0 < f_i(t) <= 1; lumped H(t) = rho(t) + (F(t) - I) tau(t)
normal_form_fit: full: lambda_i = f_i(t), b_i = 0
fault_magnitude: case 1: f_1 = f_2 = 0.2 for t > 10 s; case 2: f_1 = 0.4 + 0.2 sin(pi t), f_2 = 0.4 + 0.2 cos(pi t) for t > 10 s

metric: tracking plots only
repetitions: single run per case; no statistics

title: Self-tuning fuzzy PID-nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control for robust fault tolerant control of robot manipulators
robot_model: PUMA 560
fault_equation: qdd = M^-1(q)(tau - Xi(q, qd) - Pi(qd, tau_d)) + eta(t - T_f) phi(q, qd, tau); validation: phi_1 = 30 sin(q1 q2) + 4 cos(qd1 q2) + 15 cos(qd1 qd2) on actuator 1, phi_2 = -0.8 u_2 on actuator 2
normal_form_fit: partial: -0.8 u_2 maps to lambda_2 = 0.2; the state-dependent term on actuator 1 maps to b_1(q, qd) entering at acceleration level (through M^-1 in the paper's form)
fault_magnitude: actuator 1: 30 sin(q1 q2) + 4 cos(qd1 q2) + 15 cos(qd1 qd2); actuator 2: -0.8 u_2
onset: t = 10 s (actuator 1), t = 20 s (actuator 2)
mechanism: self-tuning fuzzy PID nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control with time-delay estimation of the lumped uncertainty and fault
detection_delay: none (no detection; TDE uses one-sample-delayed signals)
structural_condition: full actuation remains; additive and partial loss faults
platform: NR (numerical simulation of PUMA 560 model)
baselines: CTC, PID, PID-SMC, NFTSMC, PID-NFTSMC; normal-operation runs
metric: RMSE per joint and convergence time (Table 3)
repetitions: single run per controller; no statistics
notes: A_AMBIG: passive robust scheme, but TDE estimates the lumped term that includes the fault. Friction and disturbance terms present. RMSE joint 2: 0.0075 (proposed) vs 0.0164 (PID-NFTSMC).

title: Fault Tolerant Control Scheme for Robotic Manipulators Affected by Torque Faults
robot_model: 3-link planar arm with optimally fault-tolerant Jacobian (link lengths 1.41, 1.41, 0.82 m)
fault_equation: tau = tau_n + Delta_tau; multiplicative Delta_tau_i = -beta(t) tau_n,i, beta in [0,1]; failure Delta_tau_i = -tau_n,i; additive Delta_tau_i = -a_i(t); saturation Delta_tau_i = -tau_n,i + sign(tau_n,i) tau_i,max
normal_form_fit: full: multiplicative lambda_i = 1 - beta(t); failure lambda_i = 0; additive b_i = -a_i(t); saturation as reduced bound u_i = tau_i,max
fault_magnitude: bias 10 % of the maximum nominal torque on joint 1 or joint 2; 5 % and 8 % on joints 1 and 2 together; sine of frequency 1/pi with the same amplitudes
onset: NR (shown only in plots)
mechanism: first-order sliding mode unknown-input observer estimates the torque fault; estimated joint velocity loss is added in the pseudo-inverse kinematic controller of the redundant arm
detection_delay: threshold tuned for maximum detection time 0.1 s; estimation delay about 0.15 s (time-varying case)
structural_condition: kinematic redundancy degree 1 with optimally fault-tolerant design; partial torque loss
platform: NR (numerical simulation)
injection: simulated only (additive torque on named joints)
